prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1318; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured reports stopped at red light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. No injuries reported at scene by either driver; insured later reports neck and lower back discomfort.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from insured. Describes sudden impact and immediate stiffness. Confirms vehicle was driven from scene and has been inspected by a body shop. Photos of damage uploaded to file. Liability appears clear based on account and damage pattern.

Entry 3: Third-party claimant has retained counsel. All further contact to be routed through attorney's office. Letter of representation received and logged. Requested medical authorization and records for treatment since the collision, along with prior treatment history for the same body region.

Entry 4: Medical file received showing initial evaluation with diagnosis of lumbar strain. Treating provider recommends physical therapy and temporary activity modification. No fractures or imaging-confirmed disc involvement noted at this stage. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect soft-tissue injury profile.

Entry 5: Attorney's office responded that claimant continues physical therapy and expects to return to work on modified duty. Demand package requested with complete billing and wage documentation. Follow-up diary set for review once records are received. Claim remains open, liability accepted at fault-allocation stage, injury evaluation ongoing.
